system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
Senior Platform Engineer
Professional Summary
Platform engineer and technical lead with experience designing, building and operating AWS
infrastructure, production EKS platforms and infrastructure as code. Delivered developer-platform
improvements adopted by 14 product teams, reduced cloud costs and established service-level
objectives with product leadership. Previously supported game backends serving over a million daily
players, including capacity planning for major launches.
Technical Skills
Cloud infrastructure: AWS, EKS, ECS, RDS, SQS, S3, EC2, AWS Spot
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Service deployment: Kubernetes, Helm, Argo CD, ApplicationSets, GitHub Actions
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Alertmanager, Grafana, Sloth, PagerDuty, SLOs,
burn-rate alerts, capacity planning, k6
Development: Go, Python, controller-runtime
Technical leadership: Platform design, developer enablement, stakeholder collaboration, mentoring
Professional Experience
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd | 2022-Present
Technical lead of the platform team, covering the EKS platform, internal developer platform, SLOs
and cloud costs.
• Built golden-path service templates in Go and Python, Argo CD ApplicationSets and Crossplane
compositions for RDS, SQS and S3 provisioned through pull requests. Reduced time from new
service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day; adopted by all 14 product
teams.
• Used EKS, Helm, Terraform, GitHub Actions and the Backstage catalog to support the internal
developer platform.
• Replaced cluster-autoscaler-managed node groups with Karpenter and introduced AWS Spot for
stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38%, approximately GBP
410,000 annually.
• Established SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services using Prometheus recording
rules and Sloth. Reduced weekly pages by approximately 60% and agreed an error budget policy
with product leadership.
• Mentored three backend engineers transitioning into SRE.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | 2019-2022
• Supported game backends during launches with over a million daily players; operated production
EKS from 2020.
• Moved AWS infrastructure fully into Terraform with Atlantis and replaced Nagios alerting with
Prometheus and Alertmanager.
• Led capacity planning for two major launches. In 2020, used k6 load tests simulating 300,000
concurrent players to identify and fix a connection pool limit before launch.
Additional Projects and Contributions
Open-source Kubernetes cleanup controller | 2024
• Built a Go controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; approximately
120 GitHub stars.
UK DevOps meetup speaker | 2024
• Presented "SLOs that product managers care about".
Certification
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
engagement. Your scope combines cloud infrastructure design, technical ownership and
support for backend developers taking services into production. These are central to my work
as Senior Platform Engineer and technical lead at Tallybrook, where I work on the AWS EKS
platform, internal developer platform, reliability and cloud costs.
At Tallybrook, I built golden-path service templates and pull-request-based infrastructure
provisioning using Terraform, Crossplane and Argo CD. The platform was adopted by all 14
product teams and reduced the time from new service to production from approximately two
weeks to under one day. That experience is directly relevant to helping your backend
developers deploy services that are straightforward to operate. I also replaced existing node
groups with Karpenter and introduced Spot capacity with interruption handling, reducing
EC2 spend by 38%, approximately GBP 410,000 annually.
For a platform connecting on-board systems with backend services, observability and
preparation matter as much as deployment. I established SLOs and burn-rate alerts for our 20
most critical services, reduced weekly pages by approximately 60% and agreed an error budget
policy with product leadership. Previously, at Brightwater Games, I moved AWS
infrastructure fully into Terraform with Atlantis and led capacity planning for two major
launches. Load tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players exposed a connection pool limit
that we fixed before launch. These projects required turning operational risks into concrete
engineering decisions and making reliability understandable to stakeholders.
I would bring this combination of hands-on AWS infrastructure work, developer enablement
and technical leadership to Corvale’s fleet connectivity platform. I would welcome a
conversation about how my experience could support your architecture decisions and the path
from initial design to production.
Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
